formNote: Mojidata IDS: ⿱知日. 智 is 知, “to know”, with 日 below; in early texts 知 often writes the word itself.
summary: Wisdom as discernment: knowing right from wrong. Mencius found its sprout in the heart that tells 是 from 非; in Buddhist translation 智 renders jñāna, and with 慧 makes 智慧, wisdom.
placement: On the right of the disk, opposite 義. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: The Sprout of Wisdom
satellites.evidence: Mencius 2A6: 是非之心，智之端也 — “the heart that tells right from wrong is the sprout of wisdom.” 是 and 非, “this” and “not”, are the same pair as 是 and 彼 on 二’s card.

satellites.title: Knowing, Under the Sun
satellites.evidence: Mojidata IDS: 智 is 知 over 日. The graph for wisdom contains the graph for knowing.

satellites.title: Knowledge, and Wisdom’s Other Word
satellites.evidence: In Buddhist translation 智 renders jñāna, knowledge; the Abhidharmakośa’s seventh chapter, 分別智品, is its treatise on the kinds of knowing. Prajñā, the wisdom of the Perfection of Wisdom, is usually 慧 instead, or the sound loan 般若 in the Heart Sutra’s title.
satellites.caveat: A tendency, not a rule: translators also join the two as 智慧, and usage varies from one translator to another.
